issues.description:
Method: Farm.addAnimal(Animal)
Problem statement (UML) declares addAnimal(animal: Animal): boolean (returns boolean). The solution implementation (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java) defines addAnimal as 'public void addAnimal(Animal animal)' (returns void). The template file does not provide an addAnimal signature (only a TODO comment), and the textual task description describes addAnimal(Animal a) as adding an animal without specifying a boolean return, implying a void return. This mismatch between the UML return type (boolean) and the solution's signature (void) can confuse students about the expected method signature and whether they should implement a boolean return value or a void method.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the specification consistent. Preferred fix (preserves textual intent and solution): update the UML in problem_statement.md to show addAnimal(animal: Animal): void and clarify in the task text that addAnimal does not return a value. Alternatively, if you prefer a boolean return, change the solution and template to implement 'public boolean addAnimal(Animal animal)' and document the boolean semantics (e.g., return true if added).
